Technical Textiles for Clothtech Applications including Narrow Fabrics and Braids Sectional Committee,

FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized 
by the Technical Textiles for Clothtech Applications including Narrow Fabrics and Braids Sectional Committee 
had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 


Cotton tapes are made from 100 percent natural unbleached cotton yarn, mercerization of cotton tapes is performed 
in NaOH and tapes are subsequently used in berets. 


This standard, first published in 1972, and subsequently revised in 1989.This standard has been revised again to 
incorporate the following major changes: 


a) Title of the standard has been modified; 

b) The tolerance for the cotton yarn used for the manufacturing of cotton tapes has been incorporated; 

c) Relaxation on values of mass and breaking load has been incorporated for tapes manufactured from dyed 
yarns; 

d) References to Indian Standard given in Annex A has been updated; and 

e) Sampling requirement and criteria for conformity have been modified keeping in view the practical 
difficulties. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 6672 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — COTTON TAPES FOR BERETS, 
MERCERIZED — SPECIFICATION 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the constructional 
particulars and other requirements of braided cotton 
tapes used in the manufacture of berets. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards listed in Annex A. 


3 MANUFACTURE 
3.1 Yarn 


The braided cotton tape shall be manufactured from 
mercerized cotton yarn of nominal count 15 tex x 2 
(or 40 s/2) and the cotton yarn used in manufacturing 
of braided cotton tapes shall be subjected to the 
following tolerance: 


+5 
a) 0 percent on average value. 


3.1.1 The barium activity number of the mercerized 
yarn shall be not less than 160 when determined as 
per IS 1689 


3.2 Tape 


The tape shall be manufactured on a 33 spindle 
braiding machine with two ends working as one. It 
shall be flat braided under even tension with uniform 
and firm selvedges. The weave shall be as agreed to 
between the buyer and the manufacturer. 


3.2.1 It shall be free from major braiding defects 
listed at Annex B. 


3.2.2 It shall also be free from sizing, filling and 
dressing materials and substance liable to cause 
subsequent tendering. 


3.3 Dyeing 


When required, the tape shall be manufactured from 
dyed yarns. Sulphur dyes shall not be used. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 
4.1 Physical 


The tape shall conform to the physical requirements 
specified in Table 1. 


4.2 The tape shall also conform to the requirements 
specified in Table 2. 


4.3 Sealed Sample 


If in order to illustrate or specify properties of the 
tape not covered in the standard, a sample has been 
agreed and sealed, the supply shall be in conformity 
with sample in such respect. 


4.3.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a 
matter of prior agreement between buyer and seller. 


5 MARKING 


5.1 Each roll of tape shall be marked with the 
following information: 


a) Manufacturer’s name, initials or trademark 
if any; 
b) Year of manufacture; and 


c) Any other information/instruction provided 
by the manufacturer/required under law. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 PACKING 


6.1 Tapes shall be packed as per the agreement 
between buyer and seller. 


7 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY

Unless otherwise agreed, the number of rolls to be 
selected at random shall be as given in Table 3.

(Clause 3.2.1) 


LIST OF MAJOR BRAIDING DEFECTS 


a) Breaks in one or more sheath ends; 

b) Badly made knots in yarn; 

c) Loops in yarns; 

d) Frequent knots; 

e) Tight or slack braiding; and 

f) Mechanical damage, cuts, frayed portion.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: TXD 39 (20359).
